newsitem.title: USA: Northeast Utilities execs urged to step down - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Northeast Utilities execs urged to step down - WSJ.

text.p: A review of Northeast Utilities by the state of Connecticut blasted its top management for the company's poor nuclear safety record and called for the resignation of executives and senior managers responsible for problems that have closed four of the company's reactors, one of them permanently, The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.

An independent audit ordered by the state appears to make it less likely the utility will recover from consumers a significant portion of the $800 million in costs associated with the shutdown of three nuclear reactors, the story says.
The state has no authority to order personnel changes in the company and the report does not name the executives it believes should resign, the story says.

A Northeast spokesman is quoted as saying the company eased out its second-highest-ranking executive and appointed a new head of nuclear operations. Other personnel reviews are under way, the story says.
